title: Pointwise Conditional Complier Effects under Shrinking Compliance and Rough Instrument Adjustment
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision PASS; general referee tier subfield below field floor, paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4, salvageable=false. Independent validity gate confirms no faithful same-scope field repair; operator-directed downgraded stop.
gap_reasons: The displayed proofs deliver matching original-record MSE and finite honest-length orders, including saturation, but only for scalar uniform design and the single smoothness configuration alpha=beta=1/8, gamma=1.
These scope and practical-evidence limitations constrain the projected paper score even after faithful editorial repair.

The TL;DR, setup handles, and Honest scope are stale: they defer the frontier and information comparison to nonexistent Open-ended Questions despite the supplied proofs, rather than overstating an unresolved result.

No F stage ran and no Lean certification or reusable Lean promotion is claimed; stale TL;DR/setup/Honest-scope references to resolved open questions remain disclosed editorial debt.
tldr: A smooth conditional effect among compliers is identified by a conditional Wald ratio, yet rough unknown instrument adjustment can mask its shrinking observed contrasts. The focal object is the complete original-record pointwise precision frontier, jointly for minimax squared error and finite \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval length, throughout \(n\ge2\) and \(0<\delta\le1/16\). Local pair covariance projections provide a feasible upper mechanism. Continuous overlapping-sign mixtures provide a same-class lower mechanism that preserves smooth normalized complier endpoints. The frontier, its consistency boundary, the cost of unknown propensity, and the value of joint uptake-outcome information remain explicit derivation questions.
gap: Conditional IV learners establish useful upper or limit results, but those results do not give a matching pointwise risk and finite honest-length frontier with constants uniform in shrinking compliance and rough unknown adjustment.
fill: An evaluated attainable frontier and original-likelihood converse would convert weak conditional compliance into a precise sample-size and interval-width benchmark for conditional clinical IV analysis.
